gaps.concept: Whipple triad requires symptoms, documented low plasma glucose during symptoms, and relief when glucose is corrected.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes true hypoglycemia from symptoms without a measured low glucose.

gaps.concept: Hyperglycemia causes osmotic diuresis, producing polyuria, polydipsia, tachycardia, hypotension, and prerenal azotemia.
gaps.why_tested: Explains vital signs and laboratory findings in a patient presenting with DKA or HHS.

gaps.concept: Measured sodium falls as hyperglycemia draws water into extracellular fluid; corrected sodium rises about 1.6 mEq/L per 100 mg/dL glucose above 100.
gaps.why_tested: Enables interpretation of apparent hyponatremia in a hyperglycemic crisis.

gaps.concept: Effective serum osmolality is approximately 2 × measured sodium + glucose/18; urea is excluded because it crosses cell membranes.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies hypertonicity underlying neurologic symptoms in HHS.

gaps.concept: DKA typically has pH <7.3 and bicarbonate <18 mEq/L; HHS usually has pH ≥7.3 and bicarbonate ≥18 mEq/L.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes the two emergencies when glucose is markedly elevated.

gaps.concept: Urine nitroprusside tests detect acetoacetate but miss beta-hydroxybutyrate, potentially underestimating early DKA and appearing worse during recovery.
gaps.why_tested: Explains a weak urine ketone result despite severe ketoacidosis, or persistent ketonuria after improvement.

gaps.concept: Anion gap equals sodium minus chloride plus bicarbonate: Na − (Cl + HCO3).
gaps.why_tested: Requires calculation of the metabolic disturbance from an electrolyte panel.

gaps.concept: DKA can be the first presentation of type 1 diabetes; DKA and HHS can overlap in the same patient.
gaps.why_tested: Prevents classification based only on age, diabetes type, or a single laboratory feature.

gaps.concept: HHS develops over days to weeks, often with greater free-water loss than DKA; focal deficits or seizures can accompany hyperosmolality.
gaps.why_tested: Supports HHS in a gradually deteriorating patient with marked dehydration and neurologic findings.

gaps.concept: In HHS, fluid replacement precedes insulin because profound volume depletion is the immediate physiologic problem.
gaps.why_tested: Tests the first treatment choice for a severely dehydrated patient with HHS.

gaps.concept: Alcohol raises hepatic NADH, inhibiting gluconeogenesis and causing fasting hypoglycemia when glycogen stores are depleted.
gaps.why_tested: Explains hypoglycemia after heavy drinking with poor food intake.

gaps.concept: Insulinoma classically causes fasting or exercise-related hypoglycemia; a supervised fast can reproduce inappropriate insulin secretion.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes insulinoma from primarily postprandial hypoglycemia.

gaps.concept: Insulinoma is a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor associated with MEN1, especially when diagnosed at a young age.
gaps.why_tested: Connects fasting hypoglycemia to other endocrine tumors or a family history of MEN1.

gaps.concept: Excess insulin suppresses ketogenesis, so beta-hydroxybutyrate is low during insulin-mediated hypoglycemia.
gaps.why_tested: Interprets a hypoglycemia panel when insulin, C-peptide, and ketone results must be reconciled.

gaps.concept: A non-islet-cell tumor secreting IGF-2 causes hypoglycemia with suppressed insulin and C-peptide despite an insulin-like effect.
gaps.why_tested: Explains hypoglycemia with low insulin markers in a patient with a large tumor.

gaps.concept: Neonatal hypoglycemia after maternal diabetes results from persistent fetal hyperinsulinemia after delivery removes the maternal glucose supply.
gaps.why_tested: Explains low glucose shortly after birth in an infant of a diabetic mother.

gaps.concept: Severe symptomatic hypoglycemia is treated with glucose if IV access is available, or glucagon when it is unavailable.
gaps.why_tested: Tests immediate treatment of an unconscious patient with a low bedside glucose.

gaps.concept: Recurrent hypoglycemia can blunt the sympathoadrenal warning response, causing hypoglycemia unawareness.
gaps.why_tested: Explains sudden neuroglycopenia without preceding tremor or palpitations in a patient with diabetes.
